about.titleLine2: at the edge of the sand.
about.lead: Dunes Insolites runs out of Sabria, a village on the last road before the Grand Erg Oriental. Everyone who guides for us grew up within sight of these dunes.
about.whyP1: Most desert trips in Tunisia are sold by the busload — forty people, one camel line, twenty minutes, back on the coach. We wanted the opposite: small groups, local guides, and enough time on the sand that the desert stops being a photo stop and starts being a place.
about.whyP2: So we run a maximum of twelve guests per departure, twice a day, from a gate ten minutes south of Douz. Every trip is timed around the light — out before the heat, or out as the sun starts to drop.
about.how1: Every guide is from Sabria, Douz, or Kebili, and paid year-round, not per trip.
about.how2: Groups cap at twelve, and we never merge two bookings to fill a departure.
about.how3: Camels work a maximum of two trips a day and rest the whole summer.
about.how4: We carry out everything we carry in — the camps leave no trace by morning.
about.how5: A share of every booking funds the Sabria school's water tank.
about.guide1Bio: Born in Sabria, raised on the dune belt. Hédi started with two camels and a pot of tea in 2018 and still leads the golden-hour caravan most evenings.
about.guide2Bio: Former rally mechanic. Yasmine sets every route in the sand sea, briefs every rider, and keeps the fleet in better shape than most road cars.
about.guide3Bio: Snowboarder turned dune rider. Karim can have someone who has never stood on a board carving a face inside ten minutes, and he films the proof.

safety.title: Safety in the sand.
safety.lead: The Sahara is forgiving if you respect it and unforgiving if you don't. Here is exactly how we run our trips.
safety.onEveryTrip1: A licensed lead guide, plus a sweep guide on any group of six or more.
safety.onEveryTrip2: Radio contact with the gate base and a satellite messenger per group.
safety.onEveryTrip3: A first-aid kit, shade sheet, and twice the water we expect anyone to drink.
safety.onEveryTrip4: Helmets, goggles, and gloves issued and checked for every quad rider.
safety.onEveryTrip5: Boards, bindings, and saddles inspected between every session.
safety.heatProtocolBody: From June to September we run only the early morning and the last hour before sunset. If the forecast at the gate reads above 44°C we stand the day down and everyone is refunded or rebooked, no questions and no fee.
safety.insuranceP1: We carry public liability cover for all guided activity. That does not replace your own travel insurance — check that yours covers quad riding and sandboarding, since some policies class them as extreme sports.
safety.insuranceP2: The nearest hospital is in Douz, twelve minutes from the gate. Every vehicle in our fleet can reach it directly from anywhere on our routes.
safety.bring1: Closed shoes you don't mind filling with sand
safety.bring2: Long sleeves and long trousers — sun, not modesty
safety.bring4: A layer for after dark; the desert drops fast once the sun is down
safety.bring5: Cash for tips if you want to; cards work at the gate for everything else
safety.faqQ1: Do I need experience to ride a quad?
safety.faqA1: No. The quads are automatic and every session starts with a briefing and a practice lap on the flat before we head into the dunes. Riders must be 16 or older and carry ID.
safety.faqQ2: Is the camel trek suitable for children?
safety.faqA2: Children from six can ride with a parent, and handlers walk beside every camel for the whole route. Below six we recommend the sunset camp visit instead — same tea, no saddle.
safety.faqQ3: What happens if the weather turns?
safety.faqA3: Sandstorms and high wind mean we cancel, and you get a full refund or a free reschedule. That call is made by the lead guide, never by the booking desk.
safety.faqA4: Closed shoes, long sleeves, and sunglasses. We hand out a chèche for your head and neck at the gate. Skip anything you would be upset to get sand into.
safety.faqQ5: Is there phone signal out there?
safety.faqA5: Patchy. Every guide carries a satellite messenger and a charged radio, and the base at the gate knows every route and expected return time.
safety.faqQ6: Can you handle dietary or medical needs?
safety.faqA6: Yes — tell us when you book. We cater vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free at the camp, and our guides are briefed on any condition you share with us.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.collectP1: When you book a trip we collect your name, email address, phone number, party size, chosen date and departure, and any pickup or dietary notes you give us. If you join the newsletter we store only your email address.
privacy.collectP2: Our servers log standard technical data — IP address, browser, and the pages you visited — for security and to keep the site working.
privacy.why1: To confirm, run, and if necessary reschedule your trip.
privacy.why2: To reach you if the weather forces a change.
privacy.why3: To meet our legal and accounting obligations in Tunisia.
privacy.why4: To send occasional trip news, only if you asked for it.
privacy.whoP: Your guide sees the details needed to run your trip. Beyond that we share data only with the providers that host our site, send our email, and process payments, and only as much as each needs. We never sell your data.
privacy.keepP: Booking records are kept for seven years, as Tunisian accounting law requires. Newsletter subscriptions are kept until you unsubscribe, which every email lets you do in one click.
privacy.rightsPre: You can ask us for a copy of your data, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete anything we are not legally required to keep. Write to
privacy.rightsPost: and we will answer within 30 days.
privacy.cookiesP: We use a single functional cookie to remember your cookie choice. We do not run advertising trackers. If we add analytics we will ask first.

terms.title: Terms & conditions
terms.bookingP: A booking is a request until we confirm it by email with a reference number. Prices are per person in euros and include guiding, equipment, and transfers from Douz and Kebili unless stated otherwise on the trip page.
terms.paymentP: Nothing is charged when you book. We take payment at the gate before departure, or by secure link if you prefer to settle in advance. Cash in dinar and cards are both accepted.
terms.cancel1: Cancel more than 24 hours before departure: no charge.
terms.cancel2: Cancel within 24 hours: 50% of the trip price.
terms.cancel3: No-show at the gate: full price.
terms.cancel4: If we cancel — weather, equipment, or anything else on our side — you choose a full refund or a free reschedule.
terms.participationP1: Quad riders must be 16 or older and carry photo ID. Camel riders under six must ride with an adult. Tell us at booking about any medical condition, pregnancy, or mobility need so we can put you on the right trip — we would rather move you than turn you away at the gate.
terms.participationP2: Our guides may refuse or stop participation for anyone under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or anyone who ignores a safety instruction. No refund is due in that case.
terms.riskP: Desert activities carry inherent risk. We manage it with briefings, equipment checks, and trained guides, but we cannot remove it. You take part at your own risk and are responsible for holding travel insurance that covers these activities.
terms.liabilityP: We carry public liability insurance for guided activity. Nothing in these terms limits our liability for death or personal injury caused by our negligence. Otherwise our liability is limited to the price of the trip.
terms.photographyP: Guides photograph and film trips and send you the results. We also sometimes use those images publicly — tell your guide at the gate if you would rather we didn't, and we won't.
terms.lawPre: These terms are governed by Tunisian law. Complaints go to
terms.lawPost: and we will answer within 14 days.
